title: PyTorch Tensor Operations Cheatsheet
name: PyTorch Tensor Operations Cheatsheet
description: A production-oriented reference for PyTorch tensor creation, properties, reshaping, memory manipulation, and device placement.

sections.title: Tensor Creation
sections.description: Construct tensors from Python sequences, NumPy arrays, zero/one/constant filled buffers, uninitialized memory, or probability distributions.

sections.title: Inspection
sections.description: Query tensor metadata such as shape, dtype, device, strides, and memory contiguity.

sections.title: Shape Operations
sections.description: Reshape, flatten, squeeze, unsqueeze, permute, or transpose tensor dimensions.

sections.title: Manipulation
sections.description: Enforce memory contiguity, clone memory, concatenate, stack, split, or gather tensor values.

sections.title: Mathematics
sections.description: Perform element-wise arithmetic, matrix multiplication, and reduction operations.

sections.title: Broadcasting
sections.description: Expand or repeat tensor dimensions with or without copying memory.

sections.title: Device Management
sections.description: Transfer tensors between CPU/CUDA/MPS devices and manage precision casting.

entries.trigger: I need to convert a Python list or tuple into a PyTorch tensor with an explicit device or data type.
entries.snippet:
import torch

data = [[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]
x = torch.tensor(data, dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu")
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Always constructs a new tensor by copying the underlying sequence data. Infers data type automatically if dtype is not provided.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Slower performance and high memory overhead when converting large Python lists inside training loops.

**Cause:** Python lists store elements non-contiguously, forcing element-by-element iteration and memory allocation.

**Quick Fix:** Convert the Python list to a NumPy array first or use pre-allocated tensors.

entries.problem: Create Tensor from Existing Data avoiding copies (torch.as_tensor)
entries.trigger: I want to wrap an existing array or tensor into a PyTorch tensor while preserving memory layout and avoiding redundant allocation.
entries.snippet:
import numpy as np
import torch

arr = np.array([1, 2, 3])
x = torch.as_tensor(arr, dtype=torch.int64)
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Avoids memory copy when the input is already a tensor or NumPy array matching target dtype and device. Allocates new memory only if data conversion or device movement is necessary.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Modifying the created tensor unexpectedly mutates the original source data array.

**Cause:** torch.as_tensor shares underlying memory with NumPy arrays or existing tensors when no conversion occurs.

**Quick Fix:** Call torch.clone() or use torch.tensor() if independent memory storage is required.

entries.problem: Create Tensor from NumPy Array with Zero-Copy (torch.from_numpy)
entries.trigger: I need to directly wrap a NumPy ndarray into a PyTorch tensor with zero-copy memory sharing.
entries.snippet:
import numpy as np
import torch

np_arr = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], dtype=np.float32)
x = torch.from_numpy(np_arr)
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Shares the same memory storage buffer between NumPy and PyTorch. The resulting tensor cannot be resized and is placed on the CPU device.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** TypeError or unexpected mutation when passing non-writable or non-contiguous NumPy arrays.

**Cause:** The input NumPy array is read-only or not stored in standard C-contiguous layout.

**Quick Fix:** Pass np.ascontiguousarray(arr) or copy the array prior to calling torch.from_numpy.

entries.trigger: I need to initialize a tensor completely filled with zero values for accumulators or buffers.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.zeros((2, 3), dtype=torch.float32)
ref = torch.empty((2, 3))
x_like = torch.zeros_like(ref)
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Explicitly initializes every memory location to zero value. zeros_like mirrors the target tensor shape, data type, and device placement unless overridden.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** High CPU or CUDA overhead when allocating zero buffers repeatedly inside loops.

**Cause:** Instantiating new memory allocations on every iteration causes unnecessary memory fragmentation and kernel launch overhead.

**Quick Fix:** Allocate the zero buffer once outside the loop and call tensor.zero_() to reset in place.

entries.trigger: I need a tensor pre-filled entirely with value 1.0 for masking, scaling, or initialization.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.ones((2, 3), dtype=torch.float32)
ref = torch.empty((2, 3))
x_like = torch.ones_like(ref)
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Allocates tensor memory and sets all values to one. Use ones_like to automatically match another tensor's attributes.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Incompatible data types when combining integer filled ones with floating point tensors.

**Cause:** Default dtype without specification inherits integer type or default float type depending on global configuration.

**Quick Fix:** Specify dtype=torch.float32 explicitly in the creator call.

entries.trigger: I need fast buffer allocation without paying the cost of memory initialization.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.empty((2, 3), dtype=torch.float32)
ref = torch.ones((2, 3))
x_like = torch.empty_like(ref)
print(x.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Allocates uninitialized storage memory instantly containing garbage values. Fastest tensor allocation method when you plan to immediately overwrite every entry.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** NaN values or non-deterministic calculation results in model forward pass.

**Cause:** Reading or performing math on uninitialized tensor memory before writing data into it.

**Quick Fix:** Ensure every index is overwritten using copy or in-place ops before reading from the tensor.

entries.trigger: I need to allocate a tensor where every entry is initialized to a specific scalar value.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.full((2, 3), fill_value=3.14, dtype=torch.float32)
ref = torch.empty((2, 3))
x_like = torch.full_like(ref, fill_value=-1.0)
print(x)
entries.minimal_notes: Fills all tensor entries with the provided scalar value. Automatically converts fill scalar to match requested tensor dtype.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Scalar truncation or loss of precision when setting floating point fill values.

**Cause:** Default dtype inference when omitted might resolve to an integer tensor matching integer inputs.

**Quick Fix:** Explicitly pass floating point data type like dtype=torch.float32.

entries.trigger: I need to initialize random tensor values using uniform, normal, or discrete integer distributions.
entries.snippet:
import torch

unif = torch.rand((2, 3))
norm = torch.randn((2, 3))
ints = torch.randint(low=0, high=10, size=(2, 3))
print(unif.shape, norm.shape, ints.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: rand samples Uniform(0, 1), randn samples Standard Normal(0, 1), and randint samples discrete integers. Always set PRNG seed for reproducible experiments.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Non-reproducible random initialization across model training runs.

**Cause:** Calling random generation functions without fixing global or local PRNG seeds.

**Quick Fix:** Use torch.manual_seed(42) or pass a explicit torch.Generator instance.

entries.trigger: I need to construct 1D sequence tensors with fixed steps or fixed point counts.
entries.snippet:
import torch

seq_step = torch.arange(start=0, end=10, step=2)
seq_line = torch.linspace(start=0.0, end=1.0, steps=5)
print(seq_step, seq_line)
entries.minimal_notes: arange generates values in half-open interval [start, end) using a fixed step. linspace generates steps evenly spaced points across closed interval [start, end].
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Off-by-one errors or floating point rounding precision bugs when specifying steps in arange.

**Cause:** Floating point accumulation errors can cause the final boundary element to be unexpectedly included or excluded.

**Quick Fix:** Use torch.linspace when specifying exact start, end, and point counts.

entries.problem: Inspect Tensor Properties (shape, dtype, device, layout, ndim, numel, stride, is_contiguous)
entries.trigger: I need to inspect tensor metadata including dimensions, data type, storage layout, and memory stride.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 3, 4)
print(f"Shape: {x.shape}, Dtype: {x.dtype}, Device: {x.device}")
print(f"Dims: {x.ndim}, Elements: {x.numel()}, Strides: {x.stride()}, Contiguous: {x.is_contiguous()}")
entries.minimal_notes: shape returns a torch.Size tuple representing dimensions. stride shows memory step sizes required to move along each dimension.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Calling .size without invocation parentheses or treating property as method incorrectly.

**Cause:** x.shape is an attribute property while x.size() is a method call, though both return torch.Size.

**Quick Fix:** Standardize on property attributes like x.shape, x.dtype, and x.device.

entries.trigger: I need to change tensor dimensions without copying memory or allocating new storage.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.arange(12)
reshaped = x.view(3, 4)
print(reshaped.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Returns a zero-copy view sharing original memory. Requires tensor to be memory contiguous before execution.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: view size is not compatible with input tensor's size and stride.

**Cause:** Calling .view() on a non-contiguous tensor produced by operations like transpose or permute.

**Quick Fix:** Call .contiguous() before calling .view(), or use torch.reshape().

entries.problem: Reshape Tensor with Copy/View Fallback (torch.reshape / reshape_as)
entries.trigger: I need to change tensor shape reliably regardless of whether underlying memory is contiguous.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 3).t()
reshaped = torch.reshape(x, (6,))
print(reshaped.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Returns a zero-copy view if tensor is contiguous, otherwise allocates a new contiguous copy. Safe fallback alternative to torch.view.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Invalidation of downstream gradient logic when expecting a shared memory view.

**Cause:** torch.reshape quietly makes a memory copy when input memory is non-contiguous.

**Quick Fix:** Use torch.view if shared memory behavior is required, or explicitly manage contiguity.

entries.trigger: I need to collapse a range of tensor dimensions into a single dimension, such as for linear layer inputs.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(32, 3, 28, 28)
flat = torch.flatten(x, start_dim=1)
print(flat.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Flattens dimensions from start_dim to end_dim into a 1D sequence. Preserves batch dimensions when start_dim=1.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Accidentally flattening the batch dimension into feature vectors.

**Cause:** Omitting start_dim defaults to flattening from dimension 0, collapsing everything to 1D.

**Quick Fix:** Pass start_dim=1 when flattening spatial or feature dimensions for neural networks.

entries.trigger: I need to insert or remove dimensions of size 1 for shape alignment or broadcasting.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(1, 3, 1, 5)
squeezed = torch.squeeze(x)
unsqueezed = torch.unsqueeze(squeezed, dim=0)
print(squeezed.shape, unsqueezed.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: squeeze removes size 1 dimensions, while unsqueeze inserts a size 1 dimension at target index. Returns zero-copy views sharing underlying storage.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Unintended squeezing of batch dimensions when batch size dynamically equals 1.

**Cause:** Calling torch.squeeze() without arguments removes all dimensions of size 1 across the tensor.

**Quick Fix:** Always pass explicit dimension argument, for example torch.squeeze(x, dim=1).

entries.trigger: I need to swap tensor axis order for channel alignment or matrix operations.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 3, 4)
permuted = torch.permute(x, (2, 0, 1))
transposed = torch.transpose(x, 0, 2)
print(permuted.shape, transposed.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: transpose swaps exactly two dimensions. permute reorders all tensor dimensions according to provided index tuple. Returns a non-contiguous view.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Downstream memory operations fail after dimension permutation.

**Cause:** Permuting or transposing changes tensor strides, rendering memory non-contiguous.

**Quick Fix:** Chain .contiguous() immediately following .permute() or .transpose() if view operations follow.

entries.trigger: I need to force non-contiguous memory storage into contiguous order in memory.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 3).t()
print(x.is_contiguous())
x_contig = x.contiguous()
print(x_contig.is_contiguous())
entries.minimal_notes: Returns self if tensor is already contiguous, otherwise allocates new memory copy stored sequentially. Required prior to calling operations like .view().
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Unnecessary memory allocation and slow performance inside performance critical loops.

**Cause:** Calling .contiguous() on tensors that are already contiguous.

**Quick Fix:** Check x.is_contiguous() before forcing contiguous calls or use torch.reshape.

entries.trigger: I need an independent copy of a tensor that preserves autograd computation graphs.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 2, requires_grad=True)
y = torch.clone(x)
loss = y.sum()
loss.backward()
print(x.grad)
entries.minimal_notes: Allocates fresh underlying memory while preserving gradient flow back to original input tensor. Safer alternative to shallow copies or direct assignments.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Gradients leak into cloned variables or unexpected memory bloat occurs.

**Cause:** Using torch.clone() when gradient tracking is unnecessary or detached memory was intended.

**Quick Fix:** Use .detach().clone() when an isolated tensor completely outside the autograd graph is needed.

entries.trigger: I need to join multiple existing tensors along a specific existing dimension.
entries.snippet:
import torch

a = torch.randn(2, 3)
b = torch.randn(2, 3)
out = torch.cat([a, b], dim=0)
print(out.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Joins tensors along an existing dimension without creating new dimensions. All tensor shapes except target dim must match exactly.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: Sizes of tensor buffers must match except along dimension.

**Cause:** Attempting to concatenate tensors whose non-concatenated dimensions do not align.

**Quick Fix:** Verify shapes with tensor.shape and align dimensions using unsqueeze or broadcasting first.

entries.trigger: I need to combine multiple tensors along a brand new dimension.
entries.snippet:
import torch

a = torch.randn(2, 3)
b = torch.randn(2, 3)
out = torch.stack([a, b], dim=0)
print(out.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Creates a new dimension and stacks tensors along it. All input tensors must have identical shapes.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: stack expects each tensor to be equal size.

**Cause:** Trying to stack tensors with differing shape sizes across any dimension.

**Quick Fix:** Use torch.cat if joining along existing axes, or pad tensors to matching shapes.

entries.trigger: I need to divide a tensor into smaller sub-tensors along a dimension.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(10, 3)
splits = torch.split(x, split_size_or_sections=4, dim=0)
chunks = torch.chunk(x, chunks=3, dim=0)
print([s.shape for s in splits])
entries.minimal_notes: split divides into specific section sizes or uniform chunk sizes. chunk attempts to divide tensor into specified count of pieces. Returns memory views.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Unequal chunk sizes on final tensor slice.

**Cause:** Tensor length along split dimension is not evenly divisible by requested chunk size.

**Quick Fix:** Handle variable length final output chunk or pass explicit slice length list to torch.split.

entries.problem: Select and Gather Tensor Values (torch.index_select / torch.gather / torch.scatter / torch.take_along_dim)
entries.trigger: I need to collect or scatter elements using index tensors along target axes.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.tensor([[10, 20], [30, 40]])
indices = torch.tensor([[0, 0], [1, 0]])
gathered = torch.gather(x, dim=1, index=indices)
print(gathered)
entries.minimal_notes: gather extracts entries along dim specified by index tensor layout. index_select slices along a single dimension using 1D index array.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** IndexError or shape mismatch during gather operations.

**Cause:** Index tensor dimensionality or size does not match target input tensor dimensions.

**Quick Fix:** Ensure index tensor has identical number of dimensions as input tensor before calling gather.

entries.problem: Element-wise Arithmetic (add, sub, mul, div, add_)
entries.trigger: I need to perform basic element-wise mathematical operations with optional in-place modification.
entries.snippet:
import torch

a = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0])
b = torch.tensor([3.0, 4.0])
c = torch.add(a, b)
a.add_(b)
print(c, a)
entries.minimal_notes: Trailing underscores denote in-place ops like add_() that modify storage directly. Out-of-place operations allocate and return new tensors.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: a view of a leaf Variable that requires grad is being modified in-place.

**Cause:** Executing in-place arithmetic (like add_) on gradient-tracking leaf tensors.

**Quick Fix:** Use out-of-place operations (c = a + b) or disable gradient calculation when mutating.

entries.trigger: I need to compute matrix multiplication, batch matrix products, or vector dot products.
entries.snippet:
import torch

a = torch.randn(2, 3)
b = torch.randn(3, 4)
c = torch.matmul(a, b)

batch_a = torch.randn(10, 2, 3)
batch_b = torch.randn(10, 3, 4)
batch_c = torch.bmm(batch_a, batch_b)
print(c.shape, batch_c.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: mm handles strict 2D matrices, bmm handles 3D batch matrices, and matmul supports broadcasted multi-dimensional matrix products. Prefer matmul or @ operator for general code.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: Expected 2D tensor, got 3D tensor when calling torch.mm.

**Cause:** Passing batched 3D tensors into non-batched matrix multiplication primitive torch.mm.

**Quick Fix:** Use torch.bmm for explicitly 3D batches or torch.matmul for generalized dimension support.

entries.problem: Reduction Operations (torch.sum / torch.mean / torch.max / torch.min / torch.argmax)
entries.trigger: I need to aggregate tensor values across dimensions or locate extreme values.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
total = torch.sum(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
max_val, max_idx = torch.max(x, dim=1)
print(total.shape, max_val, max_idx)
entries.minimal_notes: Reductions accept dim to collapse specific axes. Pass keepdim=True to retain original dimension rank for clean broadcasting.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Broadcaster shape mismatch following reduction operations.

**Cause:** Dimension reduction collapses target axis by default (keepdim=False), altering tensor rank.

**Quick Fix:** Pass keepdim=True when planning to combine reduced tensor with original shape.

entries.trigger: I need element-wise conditional evaluation or multi-dimensional coordinate grids.
entries.snippet:
import torch

cond = torch.tensor([True, False, True])
x = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
y = torch.tensor([-1.0, -2.0, -3.0])
out = torch.where(cond, x, y)
print(out)
entries.minimal_notes: where(condition, x, y) selects elements from x when true, otherwise y. Supports broad element-wise conditions and tensor broadcasting.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Unexpected output data types or device mismatch errors in conditional outputs.

**Cause:** x and y tensors located on differing devices or having unaligned scalar data types.

**Quick Fix:** Move x and y tensors to matching devices and align dtype parameters before calling where.

entries.trigger: I need to expand single-dimensional sizes without copying tensor memory.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.tensor([[1], [2], [3]])
expanded = x.expand(3, 4)
print(expanded.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Creates a new view with expanded singleton dimensions by setting stride values to 0. Extremely fast with zero memory copy footprint.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: Expanding non-singleton dimension.

**Cause:** Passing target dimension sizes that do not match existing tensor shape at non-singleton axes.

**Quick Fix:** Only expand dimensions that currently have a size of 1, or use repeat for arbitrary copying.

entries.trigger: I need to duplicate tensor data repeatedly along specified axes by allocating physical memory.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3])
repeated = x.repeat(2, 3)
print(repeated.shape)
entries.minimal_notes: Copies tensor data physically along specified repetition counts. Unlike expand, allocates brand new underlying memory storage.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** Excessive memory consumption or slow speed on large tensors.

**Cause:** Using .repeat() when zero-copy broadcasting via .expand() or automatic broadcasting is sufficient.

**Quick Fix:** Replace .repeat() with .expand() whenever memory duplication is not explicitly required.

entries.problem: Device Placement and Dtype Conversion (to, cpu, cuda, mps, float, half, bfloat16, non_blocking)
entries.trigger: I need to move tensors between devices (CPU/CUDA/MPS) or convert primitive precision data types.
entries.snippet:
import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 3)
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
x_dev = x.to(device=device, dtype=torch.float16, non_blocking=True)
print(x_dev.device, x_dev.dtype)
entries.minimal_notes: .to() handles both device transfer and data type casting in a single call. Setting non_blocking=True enables asynchronous host-to-device memory transfers with pinned memory.
entries.common_bug:
**Issue:** RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device.

**Cause:** Performing arithmetic operations between tensors residing on different devices (e.g., CPU and CUDA).

**Quick Fix:** Ensure all operation operands are explicitly transferred to target device via .to(device).
